titulo: How Does Drinking Alcohol Affect Your Health?

fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: Past research suggested drinking alcohol in moderate amounts could be good for the heart. But a growing number of public health experts now advise people to limit alcohol intake as much as possible to improve health.

One of those experts is Dr. Timothy Naimi. He is with the Canadian Institute for Substance Use Research at the University of Victoria in British Columbia. Naimi told The Associated Press, "Drinking less is a great way to be healthier."

Earlier this month, U.S. Surgeon General Dr. Vivek Murthy called for changing his agency’s existing health warning on alcoholic drinks to include cancer risks. Such a change would require approval from Congress.
The Surgeon General’s proposed change is linked to research suggesting that drinking alcohol raises the risk of several types of cancer – including colon, liver, breast, mouth and throat.
Alcohol breaks down in the body into a substance called acetaldehyde. This chemical can damage cells and stop them from repairing themselves. The process can create conditions for cancer to grow.

Naimi said estimates show thousands of U.S. deaths could be prevented each year if people followed government dietary guidelines on drinking alcohol. The guidelines advise men to limit themselves to two drinks or fewer per day and women to one drink or fewer per day. An example of one drink would be equal to one 12-ounce can of beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine or one serving of liquor.

U.S. Surgeon General Murthy noted there are about 100,000 alcohol-related cancer cases in the United States each year. And, about 20,000 alcohol-related cancer deaths are reported yearly. "As you consider whether or how much to drink, keep in mind that less is better when it comes to cancer risk," Murthy wrote on the social media service X.

Medical experts say the idea that moderate drinking can cause health improvements, or benefits, came from imperfect studies. The research compared groups of people based on how much they drank, with amounts usually measured at only one point in time. Since some earlier studies did not follow rules about what groups were measured, researchers say they did not effectively prove cause and effect.

Naimi said people who report drinking moderately generally have higher levels of education, higher earnings and better resources for health care. He explained that when those elements are considered, “The benefits tend to disappear."

Another problem, Naimi noted, was that most studies did not include younger people. Almost half of people who die from alcohol-related causes do so before the age of 50. Naimi said the studied groups did not effectively represent all drinkers. This likely created “an appearance” of a benefit for moderate drinkers that is not real, he added.
Health guidelines related to alcohol intake have wide differences from country to country. But the overall message today is that drinking less is better for health.

Britain, France, Denmark, Holland and Australia recently examined new evidence and lowered their guidelines for safe amounts of alcohol. Ireland plans to begin requiring cancer warnings on alcohol containers starting in 2026.

Carina Ferreira-Borges is an adviser on alcohol for the World Health Organization in Europe. She said scientists had changed their minds from earlier research. This is because more recent studies suggest drinking alcohol is linked “to over 200 health conditions, including cancers, cardiovascular diseases and injuries."
titulo_es: How does drinking alcohol affect your health?
resumen_es: Public health experts are abandoning the idea that moderate drinking is beneficial: the text explains the link between alcohol and cancer, the flaws in older studies and the tightening of guidelines in several countries.

ideas_clave.idea: Contrary to earlier claims that moderate drinking benefits the heart, more and more experts now recommend reducing alcohol consumption as far as possible.
The US Surgeon General wants alcohol labels to warn about cancer, since drinking increases the risk of several types of the disease; this would need Congress's approval.
In the body, alcohol turns into acetaldehyde, which damages cells and prevents their repair, paving the way for cancer.
Following official drinking limits could save thousands of lives a year, given that alcohol is linked to some 100,000 cancer cases and 20,000 cancer deaths annually in the US.
The supposed benefits of moderate drinking stemmed from flawed studies that ignored drinkers' higher income and education and left out younger people, creating a false impression.
Although national guidelines vary, several countries have recently lowered their safe limits, and Ireland will require cancer warnings on alcohol from 2026.
The WHO notes that scientists have changed their view, as alcohol is now linked to more than 200 health conditions.

resumen_modelo: The text explains that public health experts are abandoning the long-held belief that moderate drinking is good for the heart and now advise people to drink as little as possible. In the United States, the Surgeon General has proposed adding cancer warnings to alcoholic drinks, since alcohol is broken down into a substance that damages cells and raises the risk of several cancers, causing thousands of deaths every year. According to specialists, the apparent benefits of moderate drinking came from flawed studies that measured consumption only once, ignored the higher income and education of moderate drinkers and excluded younger people. Consequently, several countries have lowered their recommended limits, and Ireland will introduce cancer warnings on labels. The World Health Organization now links alcohol to over 200 health conditions.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Earlier research suggested that moderate drinking could benefit the heart.
preguntas.cita: Past research suggested drinking alcohol in moderate amounts could be good for the heart.
preguntas.explicacion: The text starts precisely from that old idea in order to explain that it is now being questioned.

preguntas.pregunta: What would be needed to change the health warning on alcoholic drinks in the US?
opciones: A decision by the Surgeon General alone
A recommendation from the World Health Organization
A vote by the alcohol industry
preguntas.cita: Such a change would require approval from Congress.
preguntas.explicacion: The change needs the approval of Congress; the Surgeon General can only propose it. According to the text, the WHO and the industry play no part.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 2 an expression that means “asked for, demanded”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'publicly demanded or requested'.
preguntas.cita: Dr. Vivek Murthy called for changing his agency’s existing health warning
preguntas.explicacion: “To call for” means to ask for or demand publicly; do not confuse it with “to call” (to phone or to name).

preguntas.pregunta: Explain how alcohol can lead to cancer, according to the text.
respuestas: When the body breaks down alcohol, it produces acetaldehyde, a chemical that damages cells and stops them from repairing themselves, which creates conditions in which cancer can develop.
preguntas.cita: This chemical can damage cells and stop them from repairing themselves.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer must mention acetaldehyde, cell damage and the inability to repair it as the mechanism that favours cancer.

preguntas.pregunta: What do US dietary guidelines advise for women?
opciones: One drink or fewer per day
Two drinks or fewer per day
Five drinks or fewer per week
respuestas: One drink or fewer per day
preguntas.cita: women to one drink or fewer per day
preguntas.explicacion: For women the limit is one drink a day at most; two is the limit for men. The other options do not appear in the text.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: There are about 100,000 alcohol-related cancer deaths each year in the United States.
preguntas.cita: about 20,000 alcohol-related cancer deaths are reported yearly
preguntas.explicacion: 100,000 is the number of alcohol-related cancer cases; deaths are about 20,000 a year.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are earlier studies on moderate drinking considered imperfect?
opciones: Because they only studied heavy drinkers
Because they measured drinking at only one point in time and did not prove cause and effect
Because they were paid for by the alcohol industry
Because they were carried out only in Canada
respuestas: Because they measured drinking at only one point in time and did not prove cause and effect
preguntas.cita: with amounts usually measured at only one point in time
preguntas.explicacion: The studies measured drinking at a single point in time and did not prove causation. Industry funding and geographical scope are not mentioned, and they compared groups according to how much they drank, not only heavy drinkers.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 8 a word that means “income”.
preguntas.cita: higher levels of education, higher earnings and better resources for health care
preguntas.explicacion: “Earnings” is the money earned, usually from work; for companies, profits.

preguntas.pregunta: Why might moderate drinkers appear healthier than others, even if alcohol does not benefit them?
respuestas: Because people who say they drink moderately tend to be better educated, earn more and have better access to health care; once these factors are taken into account, the apparent benefits disappear.
preguntas.explicacion: An inference question about confounding variables: better health is explained by socio-economic status, not by alcohol.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Almost half of people who die from alcohol-related causes are under 50.
preguntas.cita: Almost half of people who die from alcohol-related causes do so before the age of 50.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says so, and that is why it criticises the fact that the studies did not include young people.

preguntas.pregunta: Which country plans to require cancer warnings on alcohol containers from 2026?
preguntas.cita: Ireland plans to begin requiring cancer warnings on alcohol containers starting in 2026.
preguntas.explicacion: It is Ireland. France, Denmark and Australia appear among the countries that have lowered their recommended limits, not among those that will require warnings.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Spain has also lowered its guidelines for safe amounts of alcohol.
preguntas.explicacion: The text mentions the United Kingdom, France, Denmark, the Netherlands and Australia, but says nothing about Spain.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 12 an expression that means “changed their opinion”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'adopted a different opinion'.
preguntas.cita: She said scientists had changed their minds from earlier research.
preguntas.explicacion: “To change one’s mind” means to change one’s opinion; the possessive agrees with the subject (their minds).
